question: Can the doors and windows be placed in Revit through an MCP server, and how close do E2's predictions land, at 1 cm as the round trip?

counts.server: revit_batch_mcp.py: own minimal MCP server (stdio, 4 tools); commit applied by one click on the E3 Place pyRevit button in the open, licensed Revit 2027

notes: One model only (Autodesk sample): a smoke test of the assembly step through MCP.
"truth" places the source model's own doors and windows through MCP: it tests the route, not a prediction. "transformer" places E2's predictions (type, host, place on the wall); their level is given.

The MCP client sends one place_family_instance call per element (107), then commit and extract. Commit writes the queue to a job file and waits; one click on the E3 Place pyRevit button in the open Revit applies it: opens out/rebuilt.rvt in the background, deletes its doors and windows, places the queue on the host wall given by id, saves as out/e3/e3-<run>.rvt, closes, and runs extract.py. A person triggers each commit; the placements themselves come only from the MCP calls.

First attempt, failed: the open-source Demolinator/revit-mcp-server over pyRevit Routes. On Revit 2027 with pyRevit 6.5.5 its extension startup never ran (no route registered) and Revit closed twice on a Routes worker-thread error. Its place_family also hosts on the nearest wall in 3D and cannot take a host id.

Second attempt, failed: this server (revit_batch_mcp.py) in its pyrevit-run mode, starting a batch Revit; Revit stopped at start with "The License Manager is not functioning" (education licence), so the commit moved to the button in a Revit opened by hand.
revit_messages are what Revit reported during the run (deleting and placing), counted as reported; their cause per element is not checked.
Hand and facing flips are not predicted: the transformer run leaves the family default.
Control: rebuild.py, with no AI, from pipeline/out/summary.json.
transformer: 6 of 107 not in the saved model: 5 rolled back by Revit, 1 not found after extraction.

Validity, transformer: Revit accepted 102 of 107 predicted placements and rolled the rest back; during the run it reported overlapping inserts, inserts in conflict with joined walls and instances not cutting anything (revit_messages), not checked per element. Type and host counts are over the 101 found after saving.
